extracted.intended_audience: Developers contributing Python/Cython code, documentation, and tests to the SageMath library
extracted.subtask_description: Conventions and required standards for writing/organizing Sage library code, docstrings, doctests, packaging, and ancillary files so they integrate cleanly with the Sage project and its documentation/testing infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to standard Python formatting (PEP8/PEP257)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the standard Python formatting rules when writing code for Sage as explained by PEP 8 and PEP 257.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PEP-8/PEP-257 as the baseline for formatting and docstring style. Many specific rules below are concrete instantiations of these PEPs for Sage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation: use 4 spaces, no tabs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 4 spaces for indentation levels; do not use tabs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most editors can insert 4 spaces when Tab is hit; many can replace leading tabs with 4 spaces. Exception: Makefiles require literal tab characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitespace around operators and assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use whitespace before and after assignment and binary operators of the lowest priority, but do not put whitespace for keyword argument assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good: i = i + 1; c = (a + b) * (a - b). Bad for keyword args: def f(real, imag=0.0): return magic(r=real, i=imag) (no spaces around '=' in keyword args).

rubrics_metrics.name: No whitespace immediately inside parentheses/brackets/braces
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not place spaces immediately inside ( ), [ ], or { }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., spam(ham[1], {eggs:2})[i^2 for i in range(3)] — no spaces after '(' or before ')'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Function names should be all lowercase with words separated by underscores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., def set_some_value(): ... Exceptions exist when uppercase letters make sense for historical or conventional reasons (e.g. Matrix_integer_dense.LLL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Use CamelCase for class names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factory functions that mimic constructors (e.g., PolynomialRing) are allowed and may appear like constructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Python version support policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage follows a time-window based support policy (SPEC 0) for minimum supported Python versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for a Python release is dropped 3 years after its initial release. See SPEC 0 for the exact drop schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Files and directory layout conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage source tree follows a specific layout (SAGE_ROOT/src/sage/ etc.); Python library code goes into src/sage/; directory names may be plural and filenames are usually singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A package directory should usually contain __init__.py and an all.py listing user-facing imports. Adding new top-level packages under sage should be done sparingly; prefer subpackages of existing ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose package API via all.py and prefer lazy_import
rubrics_metrics.description: User-facing items for a package should be listed in that package's all.py; prefer using lazy_import to populate all.py.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: from sage.misc.lazy_import import lazy_import; lazy_import('sage.measure_theory.borel_measure','BorelMeasure') and then add from sage.measure_theory.all import * into SAGE_ROOT/src/sage/all.py.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to place non-Python and small supporting files
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Python source code and small supporting files should be placed either in the same package directory as the code (package data, accessed via importlib.resources) or an appropriate subdirectory of src/sage/ext_data/ (deprecated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred API: importlib.resources.files(package).joinpath(resource).open('rt'/'rb') or use importlib.resources.as_file() when needed outside Python. All such files must be listed in options.package_data in the distribution setup files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling large data files
rubrics_metrics.description: Large data files should not be added directly to the Sage source tree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a separate git repository, add packaging metadata to make it pip-installable, upload to PyPI, and then add metadata to SAGE_ROOT/build/pkgs so Sage knows about it. Compress files (e.g., xz -e) and read via lzma.open when needed. Examples: conway-polynomials and matroid-database repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use search_src/search_def/search_doc to learn by example
rubrics_metrics.description: When adopting conventions, look at existing Sage code and use the search_src, search_def, and search_doc commands from the Sage prompt to find examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the sage: prompt use search_src(string), search_def(string) for function definitions, and search_doc(string) for documentation. Check docstrings of those functions for conventions and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-of-file header and license
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Sage code file should start with a docstring that contains a short one-line summary (no period), a paragraph description, an EXAMPLES section, and an AUTHORS list; files must include the GPLv2+ (or compatible) license header.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include AUTHORS entries as concise lines with name (YYYY-MM-DD): short description. The authoritative author log is git blame. Include the standard GPL license block as shown in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstring: required blocks and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Every function must have a docstring containing at least a one-sentence description ending in a period and followed by a blank line; additional sections are required/strongly recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Docstring should: give a one-sentence description (command-style), optional longer description, assumptions about objects, define terms/aliases, and include INPUT and OUTPUT blocks describing arguments and return value(s). Use descriptive (not necessarily exact Python) type names; mention defaults. Use EXAMPLES block (not optional) and TESTS block (highly recommended).

rubrics_metrics.name: INPUT and OUTPUT block formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use INPUT: and OUTPUT: blocks to describe all function arguments and outputs, including types and default values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: INPUT items: list argument name in backticks, type description, default values when applicable, and descriptive notes. OUTPUT: should describe expected result (required if one-sentence description needs expansion); if multiple outputs, describe each component.

rubrics_metrics.name: EXAMPLES block requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every docstring must include an EXAMPLES block; these examples are used both for documentation and tested as doctests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide illustrative examples with good coverage of functionality. Examples are run as tests before each release. Be verbose enough to explain what examples do.

rubrics_metrics.name: TESTS block and testing corner cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a TESTS block (highly recommended) for tests not intended as examples, such as input validation and corner cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TESTS blocks are stripped from interactive help but run by the doctest framework. Use TESTS: pytest for pytest-marked tests. Provide tests for corner cases (0, empty set, null matrices) and input validation, and for interruptibility checks when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sphinx/reST directive and documentation style
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage documentation is written in reStructuredText and processed by Sphinx; use uppercase for the main Sphinx directives and follow line-length and quoting rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lines should be shorter than ~80 characters. Sphinx directives (e.g., .. NOTE::, .. WARNING::, .. MATH::) must be uppercase and written exactly as specified. Quote code fragments and literals with double backticks (``like_this``). Prefer raw triple-quoted docstrings (r"""...") and LaTeX typesetting where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master bibliography and citation keys
rubrics_metrics.description: All bibliographic references should go in the master bibliography file SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/reference/references/index.rst and citation keys should follow conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation key format: first three letters of family name + year for single author, first letters of family names + year for multiple authors; use four-digit years. Escape first-name initials with a backslash in bibliography entries to avoid list enumeration. Use [Key]_ in docstrings to create hyperlinks to master bibliography.

rubrics_metrics.name: MATH/LaTeX rules in docstrings
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeX code is allowed in docstrings, normally inline within backticks or in MATH blocks; when using LaTeX commands, prefer raw strings to avoid escaping backslashes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backslashes must be doubled unless the docstring is raw (r"""..."). MATH blocks get wrapped automatically into math environments for PDF; use :nowrap: when you need an environment unwrapped. Keep interactive-console readability in mind (LaTeX shown as code), so prefer readable forms when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing testable examples / doctest guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctests in EXAMPLES/TESTS should serve both as documentation and automated tests; they must pass under the sage -t framework and follow specific conventions for environment, tags, and behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctests should: show interesting usage, cover all meaningful argument combinations, include corner cases, ensure interruptibility when needed, and be systematic where possible. Use the sage: prompt form so examples can be copy/pasted. Use tmp_filename/tmp_dir for file output. Wrap long lines sensibly (columns ~80–88, max 95 in source), use parentheses to break lines, and do not wrap string literals. Use doctest tags and magic comments (# random, # long time, # abs tol 1e-9, # optional - feature, # needs feature, # not implemented, etc.) correctly. Align magic comment tags per style guidance (e.g., column 88 for some tags). Use 'indirect doctest' tag when calling A indirectly. Use 'nodoctest' to skip files or directories when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest flags and marker usage
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive list of doctest markers and flags are supported to control what is tested and how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: # random (don't check output), # long time (only tested with --long), # abs/rel tol N (tolerance for numerical checks), # not implemented (never tested), # optional -package and # needs package/feature (conditional testing), # optional - bug or # known bug for known failures, optional tags are case-insensitive, and words after optional/needs are parsed as package/feature names until punctuation. Place block-scoped tags immediately after the sage: prompt to apply to the whole block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sage -t to run automated doctests and which files to test
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated doctesting is performed with sage -t on .py, .pyx, .sage, and .rst files; doctests in these files should run successfully with sage -t <file>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctester uses the Sage preparsing and recognizes sage: and >>> prompts. For reST files, link verbatim environments with .. link :: and use .. linkall to connect all examples in a file. Use .. skip before an example to skip it in tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: General coding whitespace rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use spaces instead of tabs for indentation (except in Makefiles) and avoid trailing whitespace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure editors to insert spaces and remove trailing whitespace. Emacs .dir-locals.el is provided for recommended editor config; see other editor docs for similar configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private function conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions whose names start with an underscore are private; their docstrings should not contain crucial user-facing information and may be hidden from reference manuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private functions should still contain EXAMPLES or TESTS blocks. Use automethod in a public method's docstring to surface private docstrings if desired. Special-case: __init__ docstring is used as the class docstring if no class docstring exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Sphinx directives list (must be uppercase)
rubrics_metrics.description: The main Sphinx directives used in Sage are MATH, NOTE, PLOT, RUBRIC, SEEALSO, TODO, TOPIC, WARNING, etc., and must be written in uppercase exactly as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using incorrect capitalization or variants (e.g., WARNING :: vs .. WARNING::) will not work. A few other directives such as MODULEAUTHOR, automethod, autfunction, image, figure are also available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability balance for LaTeX in interactive help
rubrics_metrics.description: When writing LaTeX formulas, balance precision and readability for interactive console consumers who see the raw LaTeX code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer expressions that remain readable when shown as LaTeX code; e.g., prefer a/b or a b^{-1} over \frac{a}{b} when it improves interactive readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master bibliography reference placement and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Put bibliographic entries in the project's master bibliography file rather than in individual docstrings in most cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use REFERENCE blocks in docstrings when necessary and add the bibliographic info to the master file. Use the key format and backslash-escaped initials as described in the master file guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template usage and raw strings encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the provided template for docstrings (INPUT/OUTPUT/EXAMPLES/SEEALSO/TESTS etc.) and prefer raw string docstrings r"""...""" even if backslashes are not currently present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template shows indentation and block formatting rules. Be sure to leave a blank line after example code and before explanatory text. Illustrate exceptions in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: GlobalOptions and common keyword arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide consistency in common keyword arguments across functions and document GlobalOptions where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common keywords and semantics: algorithm (string|None): choose implementation; certificate (bool, default False): return (result, certificate); proof (bool, default True): require provable computation; check (bool): additional input checks; coerce (bool): convert input to suitable parent; inplace (bool): modify in-place or return copy. Use GlobalOptions to define class-level defaults when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-ASCII identifier transliteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate non-ASCII characters in identifiers to ASCII equivalents according to simple rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: translate ä and ö to ae and oe (moebius_function for Möbius), translate á to a (lovasz_number for Lovász). Follow these rules for identifiers to maintain portability.
